case_number: Crl. Appeal No.82474-J/2022 / Murder Reference No.331/2022 / P.S.L.A. No.82858/2022
case_type: Criminal Appeal / Murder Reference / Private Complaint / PSLA

trial_court.court_name: Additional Sessions Judge, Toba Tek Singh
trial_court.sentence: Death as Ta'zir with Rs.300,000 compensation under Section 544-A Cr.P.C.

facts.location: Killa No.11, Square No.61, Chak No.188/GB, District Toba Tek Singh
facts.summary: The appellant along with co-accused allegedly fired multiple shots at Imran due to previous enmity related to a 2015 murder case. FIR No.412/2021 was registered at Police Station Rajana. The trial court convicted the appellant while acquitting co-accused.

recovery.issue: Live bullets missing from forensic parcel creating doubt in chain of custody

legal_issues.issue: Rigor Mortis and Time of Death
legal_issues.finding: Full rigor mortis observed within five hours in month of May was medically implausible; death likely occurred earlier than stated in FIR.
legal_issues.principle: Rigor mortis is variable and influenced by temperature; inconsistency with ocular account creates doubt.

legal_issues.finding: Seminal discharge is a recognized involuntary post-mortem reflex and does not prove prior sexual activity.
legal_issues.principle: Post-mortem seminal emission has neutral medico-legal significance.

legal_issues.finding: Material improvements made in private complaint to reconcile with medical evidence; discrepancies in number of fire shots.
legal_issues.principle: Material contradictions between ocular and medical evidence weaken prosecution case.

legal_issues.finding: Close relatives allegedly present remained unharmed; Investigating Officer recorded statements contradicting their presence.
legal_issues.principle: Improbable conduct of witnesses casts doubt on presence at scene.

legal_issues.finding: Co-accused attributed similar roles were acquitted; no strong independent corroboration against appellant.
legal_issues.principle: When testimony disbelieved for some accused, requires strong corroboration to convict remaining.

legal_issues.finding: Discrepancy in forensic parcel; chain of custody compromised.
legal_issues.principle: Tampered or doubtful recovery cannot sustain conviction.

legal_issues.finding: Investigating Officer admitted motive not substantiated during investigation.
legal_issues.principle: Unproven motive further weakens prosecution case.
Single reasonable doubt sufficient for acquittal.

state: Ocular account supported by medical evidence.
Motive established due to prior enmity.
Muhammad Waqas Anwar, Deputy Prosecutor General

judgment_summary.Crl. Appeal No.82474-J/2022: Allowed; conviction and death sentence set aside; appellant acquitted
judgment_summary.Murder Reference No.331/2022: Answered in Negative; death sentence not confirmed
judgment_summary.release_order: Appellant to be released forthwith if not required in any other case

legal_references.case_name: Kanubbai Virjibhai v. State of Gujarat
Ranjit Urang v. State of Tripura
RAFAQAT ALI alias FOJI v. The State
NAJAF ALI SHAH v. The STATE
The STATE v. AHMED OMAR SHEIKH

remarks: Due to medical inconsistency regarding rigor mortis, unreliable ocular account, doubtful recovery, unproven motive, and acquittal of similarly placed co-accused, the appellant was acquitted on benefit of doubt.
